newsitem.title: USA: Augusta-Richmond Cty, Ga, to sell $75 mln revs.
newsitem.headline: Augusta-Richmond Cty, Ga, to sell $75 mln revs.

text.p: Georgia's Augusta-Richmond County government plans a $75 million water-sewer revenue bond issue on Dec 2, finance director David Collins said Tuesday.
The Robinson-Humphrey Co Inc is senior manager for the negotiated sale.

About $36 million of the issue will refund and defease water-sewer bonds issued by the county in 1986, 1997 and 1991, and water-sewer bonds issued by the City of Augusta in 1972 and 1991. The two merged last year to become the Augusta-Richmond County Consolidated Government.
The remaining new money part of the issue will finance new construction.

Since 1987, the former city government has transfered up to $10 million of waterworks revenues into the city's general fund each year to help keep the city afloat. The payments continued this year with a $6.7 million transfer.
Under terms of the new bond issue, transfers to the general fund will be capped at $1 million a year, beginning in 2000 and until the bonds are paid off in 2027.

Collins said the issue had been planned for Dec 3, a Tuesday, but that "the demand side is going to be kind of swelling up around that same day." The sale was moved to Monday, Dec 2, but the date could still change depending on market conditions and volume.
